requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading on node1 in the current boot.
requirements.summary: Before configuration, usb_storage was unloaded but loadable. After configuration, the effective install rule resolved to /bin/false, an explicit modprobe failed, and usb_storage remained unloaded.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: The policy was present in the rebuilt initramfs. A completed reboot changed the boot ID, after which the policy remained present, an explicit modprobe still failed, and usb_storage remained unloaded.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. usb-storage was directly shown to be denied in the current boot and again after a verified reboot, while node1 recovered cleanly. Evidence quality is high; only minor temporary-file residue affects operational hygiene.
limitations: No physical USB mass-storage hot-plug/autoload event was exercised; enforcement was demonstrated through explicit modprobe attempts and post-reboot module-state checks.

The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /etc/modprobe.d or initramfs contents, so persistence evidence relies on the executor's direct post-reboot commands; these observations are coherent with the independently captured boot-ID change.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task roles: installing the persistent deny policy, rebuilding initramfs, and rebooting to test persistence. The reboot protocol was strong: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the reboot, observed a different boot ID, and demonstrated recovery with a running system, zero failed units, writable root, retained policy, and blocked module. The only hygiene defect was leaving two small diagnostic output files in /tmp: /tmp/usb-storage-test.out from cmd-64dc20a92c964162 and /tmp/usb-storage-postreboot.out from cmd-131bc4b491ea4d50. They remained after execution and should have been removed. No failed services, package damage, or additional network exposure was observed.
